title: European option contracts and payoffs check

items.prompt: What right does the holder of a European call have in this lesson?

options.label: The right to buy the underlying at the strike at expiry
The right to sell the underlying at any time before expiry
An obligation to buy the underlying at expiry

items.explanation: A European call holder has a right, not an obligation, to buy at the strike at the single expiry time.

items.prompt: Who has the exercise right and who must perform if a European put is exercised?

options.label: The holder chooses; the writer must perform
The writer chooses; the holder must perform
Both sides independently choose whether to perform

items.explanation: The option premium buys the holder the exercise right; the writer bears the corresponding obligation under the stated contract.

items.prompt: Two European calls each have strike USD 100. The underlying is worth USD 115 at expiry. What is the total holder payoff in USD?
items.explanation: Each call pays max(115 - 100, 0) = USD 15. Two calls pay USD 30.

items.prompt: A trader writes three European puts with strike USD 85. The underlying is worth USD 70 at expiry. What is the writer's signed payoff in USD?
items.explanation: Each holder receives max(85 - 70, 0) = USD 15, so the writer pays 3 × 15 = USD 45 and has payoff USD -45.

items.prompt: A call is purchased today for a USD 6 premium and later pays USD 9 at expiry. Ignoring financing, which quantities are correctly labeled?

options.label: Both payoff and profit are USD 9

items.explanation: The contract payoff is USD 9. Ignoring financing, profit subtracts the USD 6 premium and is USD 3.

items.prompt: An out-of-the-money option expires with zero payoff. Does that imply its value was zero on every earlier date?

options.label: No, earlier value reflected the remaining possible future payoffs
Yes, a zero realized payoff makes every earlier value zero
Yes, option value always equals expiry intrinsic value

items.explanation: Before expiry, more than one future state may remain possible. A realized zero payoff does not retrospectively erase the value of the contingent right.
